beats.summary: Andy and the office joke about hunger and the Civil War flags, with Andy dramatizing the importance of pride and the flag.

evidence.snippet: Andy: Hunger! Hunger for victory! Hunger for honor. Hunger for pride.

beats.summary: Andy insists on continuing a walk to Spangler Springs despite others being tired and hungry, leading to a humorous moment when he looks back and finds no one following.

evidence.snippet: Phyllis: I don't think I should walk anymore.
Dwight (Andy looks back to find everyone sitting): You said you weren't going to look back.

beats.summary: Dwight and Oscar consult an archivist who reveals that the Battle of Schrute Farms was actually a peaceful artistic refuge during the Civil War.

evidence.snippet: Archivist: Schrute Farms did you say? That is a fascinating little chapter of the Civil War.

Narrator: But the Battle at Schrute Farms was no battle at all. It was a code used by pacifists from both North and South who turned the Pennsylvania farmhouse into an artistic community and a refuge from the war.

beats.summary: Kevin and Ryan argue over the origin of the 'Big Mac idea,' with Kevin accusing Ryan of stealing it, but Ryan eventually admits it was Kevin's idea.

evidence.snippet: Kevin: No! This is not fair! This is my idea. He's trying to steal it because he's jealous of me.
Ryan: You know what? Now I remember. That was your idea. That is 100 percent your idea.

beats.summary: Andy confronts Jim about the office's sarcastic attitude towards the Gettysburg trip, but Jim reassures Andy that they like him and are supporting him despite the jokes.

evidence.snippet: Andy: Our office has a disease. And it goes by many names. Sarcasm. Snark. Wisecracks.

beats.summary: Andy reflects that his analogy of the office as an army was wrong and that they are just people who work in an office with him as their manager.

evidence.snippet: Andy (voiceover the three walking): The world will little note, nor long remember the fight Jim and I had here at Gettysburg and that's good because I was basically wrong.
